# FDG8061

> AVOID using `Nullable<bool>` to represent a general three-state value.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.8 Nullable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Not machine-checkable: whether a bool? is a truly optional Boolean or a general three-state value is what it means.

## From the book

`Nullable<bool>` should only be used to represent truly optional Boolean values: true, false, and not available. If you simply want to represent three states (e.g., yes, no, cancel), consider using an enum.
